questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 ?
questions.explain: Count the 10s: there are 5 of them, so this is 5 groups of 10, which is 5 × 10 = 50. Counting one group too few gives 4 × 10, which is 10 too little, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 10 × 10 or 4 × 5. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Mei Ling works out 3414 + 3328 in columns. One column makes 12, so she writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Mei Ling works out 3414 + 3328 in columns. One column makes 12, so she writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 12 is the ones column: 4 + 8 = 12, and no other column reaches ten. 12 ones is 1 ten and 2 ones, so the 2 stays in the ones column - worth 2 - and the small 1 goes above the tens column - worth 10. The small 1 is worth 10. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stem: Xin Yi has four digit cards: 0, 3, 7, 6. She uses each card once to make a 4-digit number. What is the smallest even number she can make?
questions.stemText: Xin Yi has four digit cards: 0 , 3 , 7 , 6 . She uses each card once to make a 4-digit number. What is the smallest even number she can make?
questions.explain: An even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, so the ones card must be 0 or 6. Try each one in the ones place, and each time make the smallest number you can from the other three cards. The 0 cannot go first: a number that starts with 0 is not a 4-digit number. With 0 last: 3670. With 6 last: 3076. The smallest of these is 3076. (3067 is smaller, but it is odd, so it does not count.)

Now add up the digits of each one: 1 + 3 + 0 = 4; 2 + 6 + 0 = 8; 3 + 9 + 0 = 12. Only 130 has digits that add up to 4.

questions.stemText: At a stall at the pasar malam, tubs of cookies cost $4 each, or 5 for $18. Mei Ling needs 8 tubs of cookies. What is the least amount Mei Ling must pay? (in dollars, e.g. 4.75)
questions.explain: Buying 5 tubs of cookies one by one costs 5 × $4 = $20, but 5 for $18 is cheaper, so buy as many bundles as you can. 8 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 3, so 1 bundle cost 1 × $18 = $18. The 3 tubs of cookies left over cost 3 × $4 = $12 (cheaper than one more bundle at $18). Total: $18 + $12 = $30. Buying all 8 one by one would cost $32.

questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 19 cm long and 6 cm wide. A notch 4 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 8 cm of edge before the notch and 7 cm after it, and the banner is still 4 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 8 + 2 + 4 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 19 + 6 = 54 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 4 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 4 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (19 + 6) + 2 × 2 = 54 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
